title: Telemetry proto fanout and soft-schema translation
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a resilient telemetry inlet component that performs protocol-level fanout into multiple downstream validation/transformation lanes and applies a 'soft' schema translation layer to allow gradual schema evolution without hard rejections. This ticket covers the backend service changes needed in the console usage pipeline: a new Telemetry Fanout service (inlet-fanout) + a soft-schema translator library used by existing validators and the new canary pipeline.

Background: Our current ingestion path rejects events that fail strict schema validation or type coercion, which increases customer-facing telemetry loss during rolling changes and results in sizable backfills when schema changes are deployed by instrumenting clients. We need a path that can: preserve high-throughput characteristics, minimize tail latency regressions, and give us observability into schema drift while maintaining safety for downstream analytics and billing.

Objectives:
- Add a lightweight fanout layer at the intake boundary to duplicate ingested envelopes to: primary validation (fast strict path), canary soft-translation path, and archival raw store for reprocessing.
- Implement a soft-schema translator library that applies non-destructive coercions, attaches normalized type hints, and emits a translation report alongside the event (translation metadata) instead of rejecting.
- Expose metrics and tracing that surface translation rates, coercion types, and per-tenant drift signals to Console dashboards and alerting.

Non-goals: Full schema migration tooling (this ticket only provides translation + observability hooks, not automated migrations), UI for per-tenant schema edits (handled by PM follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: New inlet-fanout service deployed behind existing ingress with feature-flag gating
Fanout duplicates events to three lanes: strict-validator, soft-translator-canary, raw-archival; no increased 99th latency > 20ms over baseline for 95% of requests
Soft-translator library produces translation metadata attached as event.headers.translation_report with schema version hint and coercion list
Console dashboards show translation_rate, coercion_breakdown, tenant_drift_score and a Grafana panel for top 10 translators and top coercion types
Backward-compat tests covering: numeric coercion, enum fallback, missing optional fields, and unexpected nested objects
Rollout plan executed with canary traffic at 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if coercion_rate > 5% or increase in ingestion errors > 0.5%
Integration test harness can replay archived raw events through translator and produce identical translation_report for deterministic inputs
design_notes:
Architecture: inbound HTTP/gRPC -> ingress gateway -> inlet-fanout -> (strict-validator queue, soft-translator topic, raw-archival S3). The soft-translator will be library-first: we will publish a Go library (and a thin Node shim) that exports a Translate(envelope, schemaRegistryLookup) -> (envelopeWithHints, translationReport). Translation rules are expressed as prioritized rule sets in the schema registry: coercion rules, optional defaulting, enum mapping tables. We will not mutate original payload body; the translator only emits headers and a canonicalized copy to the soft topic.

Performance constraints: the translator must operate at ~50k events/s per instance when running on the existing inlet machines. To meet latency SLOs we will: implement fast-path for events matching current active schema version (no-op), cache recent schema rules, and batch lookups to the schema registry.

Failure modes & safety: if translator fails, fanout must continue delivering to strict-validator and raw-archival only. If translator raises high coercion rates for a tenant, alert and automatically divert that tenant to manual review channel.

Data retention: raw-archival retention 90d hot + cold archive for 1 year. Translation metadata stored as part of event headers in the soft topic for 30d.
api_changes: No API surface change for external customers. Internal: new header X-Telemetry-Translation-Version will be emitted for events processed by the soft-translator. Backfill/Replay API extended with query param ?replay_with_translation=true to include translation_report during replays.
rollout_plan: Deploy inlet-fanout behind feature flag (ff.telemetry_inlet_fanout) in staging
Enable canary: route 1% of production traffic to fanout and soft-translator; monitor translation_rate and latency for 24h
Gradually increase canary to 10% then 50% with fixed observation windows
Once stable, flip fanout as default and enable archival to raw-bucket
Run controlled tenant replays for the last 7 days to validate translation determinism
Post-rollout: run a 48h sweep to identify top translation anomalies and create follow-up tickets
telemetry_and_monitoring: Tracing: each event gets a trace with spans: ingress->fanout->strict-validate->soft-translate->archival; translation_report attached as span tag for sampling
Alerts: translator_error_rate > 0.2% sustained over 5m, tenant_coercion_rate > 5% for a single tenant over 1h, fanout_latency_p99 > baseline + 50ms
Dashboards: Console shows per-tenant drift-score (0..100), rolling 7d translation rates, top coercion types, and backlog depth for soft-translator topic
testing_plan: Unit tests for translator rules (coercion, enum mapping, defaulting). Local harness that replays archived raw events and asserts identical translation_report across runs. Load tests to validate 50k events/s with <2ms added median latency. Chaos tests: translator process exits and ensure fanout still delivers to strict path and raw archival. End-to-end tests with synthetic tenant that simulates a schema bump and validates alerting and tenant diversion behavior.
